subject: Mixed SEM model (binary and ordered categorical vars)

messages.author: 40b553b403fffa7c
messages.subject: Mixed SEM model (binary and ordered categorical vars)
parts:
Hello All

I am building a SEM model using lavaan and my dataset has the variables:
  • V001 and V002 are ordered factor (1,2,3,4,5) but in the dataset they are declared as numeric
  • The other variables are binary factor (0,1) also declared as num
I folowed the Lavaan tutorial here https://goo.gl/uKZP2B to build the model with categorical variables I used the the following command:

model = "V001  ~  V008            
             V002  ~  V001 + V008 + V051 + V052 + V053"
  
model.fit    <- lavaan::sem(model, data = myData, ordered =c("V001", "V002")) # declared ordered only for the two endogenous variables

So the result was:
 
lavaan (0.5-23.1097) converged normally after  26 iterations

  Number of observations                          5000

  Estimator                                                DWLS      Robust
  Minimum Function Test Statistic              253.552     249.326
  Degrees of freedom                                          3               3
  P-value (Chi-square)                                   0.000         0.000
  Scaling correction factor                                              1.017
  Shift parameter                                                           0.051
    for simple second-order correction (Mplus variant)

My doubts are:
  • the p-value (Chi-square) that was so low means my model has not a good fit right?
  • How to interpret Scaling correction factor  and Shift parameter ? They say something about the problem of fit?
  • Is there a lavaan tool to investigate the problem?
  • Are ther more practical examples with these mixed data?

Other results are:


lavaan::standardizedSolution(model.fit)
    lhs       op  rhs    est.std    se           z pvalue
1  V001   ~ V008    -0.035 0.015   -2.415  0.016
2  V002   ~ V001     0.107 0.014    7.552  0.000
3  V002   ~ V008     0.013 0.017    0.794  0.427
4  V002   ~ V051     0.054 0.015    3.513  0.000
5  V002   ~ V052     0.035 0.015    2.274  0.023
6  V002   ~ V053    -0.124 0.016   -7.778  0.000
7  V001    |      t1    -1.159 0.113  -10.252  0.000
8  V001    |      t2     0.044 0.113     0.391  0.696
9  V001    |      t3     1.209 0.115   10.558  0.000
10 V001   |      t4     2.172 0.128   16.937  0.000
11 V002   |      t1    -1.137 0.120    -9.488  0.000
12 V002   |      t2    -0.570 0.118    -4.834  0.000
13 V002   |      t3     1.633 0.118   13.835  0.000
14 V002   |      t4     2.719 0.128   21.321  0.000
15 V001  ~~ V001   0.999 0.001 976.467  0.000
16 V002  ~~ V002   0.965 0.005 209.282  0.000
17 V001 ~*~ V001   1.000 0.000        NA     NA
18 V002 ~*~ V002   1.000 0.000        NA     NA
19 V001  ~1            0.000 0.000        NA     NA
20 V002  ~1            0.000 0.000        NA     NA


lavaan::fitMeasures(model.fit)



Somebody would help please?


Thank you all
RC

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Mixed SEM model (binary and ordered categorical vars)
parts:
Your n is 5,000, so your power to detect discrepancies is fairly high.
Degrees of freedom come from constraints. The three constraints in your model are the non-paths from 
V051, V052 and V053 to V001. Your current model says that the partial correlations of these three predictors
with V001 are 0, after accounting for their covariance with V008, which does predict V001. You could use 
the modIndices function to get estimates of exactly how each constraint is affecting your chi-square. Or you 
could estimate the model including those 3 paths and then make a judgment whether they have practical 
significance.

Dear Edward

Thank you for you answer, see coments below:

Em terça-feira, 7 de novembro de 2017 14:07:57 UTC-2, Edward Rigdon escreveu:

Got it !

V051, V052 and V053 to V001. Your current model says that the partial correlations of these three predictors
with V001 are 0, after accounting for their covariance with V008, which does predict V001.

Sorry but I cannot see this. From where did you concluded that?

//
From your syntax:

model = "V001  ~  V008             
             V002  ~  V001 + V008 + V051 + V052 + V053"

V001 is not directly dependent on V051, V052, or V053
//
 
It is from these lines:

17 V001 ~*~ V001   1.000 0.000        NA     NA
18 V002 ~*~ V002   1.000 0.000        NA     NA
19 V001  ~1            0.000 0.000        NA     NA
20 V002  ~1            0.000 0.000        NA     NA
You could use

the modIndices function to get estimates of exactly how each constraint is affecting your chi-square. Or you 
could estimate the model including those 3 paths and then make a judgment whether they have practical 
significance.

OK, start reading about it.

One more doubt:
How to interpret these lines:
V001    |      t1    -1.159 0.113  -10.252  0.000
V001    |      t2     0.044 0.113     0.391  0.696

//
These are thresholds associated with ordinal variable V001. They are part of modeling an underlying 
continuous variable based on your ordinal observed variable.
//
 
and

19 V001  ~1            0.000 0.000        NA     NA
20 V002  ~1            0.000 0.000        NA     NA

//
The "1" stands for the intercept. The intercepts for V001 and V002 are 0.
//
